title: Compact proofflow & onboarding UX for customer-managed VPCs - PRD draft
content:
Purpose
- Lightweight PRD draft for a minimal proofflow and onboarding UX targeted at customer-managed VPC/private deployments. Goal: give security teams a compact, auditable snapshot (proof) of onboarding steps + an approval gate UX that minimizes friction for customers and support.

Problem statement
- Customers adopting Private deployments want a short, verifiable handoff artifact (<= 5KB compressed) that proves operator intent and key telemetry at time of onboarding. Current handoff is verbose: many logs, docs, and ad-hoc screenshots. This increases audit burden and slows SLA signoff.

Goals (MVP)
- Produce a compact evidence bundle for each onboarding event that contains: immutable step assertions, signed approval token, and a sampled telemetry digest. Target size: < 10KB ASCII or < 5KB compressed.
- Add an in-console approval gate flow for operator + customer reviewer with 2-click finalization and optional QA notes.
- Ensure all artifacts are queryable from the Platform Console and exportable to customer SIEM.
- SLOs: approval path time median < 6 hours (human), automated gating < 120s.

Non-goals
- Full-fidelity packet captures or exhaustive telemetry retention (those belong to long-term audit/archive).
- Replacing customer-side SIEM integrations — only provide export hooks and compact evidence.

High-level approach
1) Compact evidence bundle: generate a JSONL-like compact payload with fixed fields: event_id, timestamp, operator_id (hashed), customer_vpc_id, step_summary (short strings), approval_signature, telemetry_digest (SHA256 of sampled telemetry). Keep fields narrow to ensure small size.
2) Approval gate UX: embed a single-line summary + 3 expandable detail rows. Primary actions: Approve, Request Changes, Escalate. Approve creates a signed approval token stored on control plane and mirrored to customer export endpoint (S3/HTTP webhook).
3) Audit log contract: derive digest-based index that can be rehydrated to full logs on-demand from longer retention stores. The digest links to the query key in customers' long-term storage (if they opt in).

Sample compact bundle schema (conceptual, intentionally terse)
- event_id: rwi-<shortid>
- ts: 2025-01-12T15:37:22Z
- op: maya.patel (or hashed op id)
- vpc: cust-1234
- steps: ["attach-route","open-egress-approval","install-agent"] (strings, no verbose metadata)
- decision: approved | changes_requested | escalated
- signature: sig_v1(base64)
- telemetry_digest: sha256(base64)
- proof_links: [s3://cust-evidence/...] (optional)

UX flow (operator)
- Step 0: Create onboarding job — selects vpc, region, optional telemetry retention. UI shows estimated evidence bundle size.
- Step 1: Auto-run preflight checks (30–90s). Results summarized as green/yellow/red. UI condenses failures to short IDs with hover details.
- Step 2: Operator selects final checklist checkboxes (network owner confirmed, firewall rules reviewed, key rotation scheduled). Minimal fields — each checkbox maps to a single assertion in the proof bundle.
- Step 3: Operator clicks "Request customer approval" — creates a pending approval record and emits notification to customer reviewer.
- Step 4: Customer reviewer receives email + console link. They see 1-line summary, 3 expanders (network changes, telemetry digest, operator notes). They can Approve / Request changes / Escalate. Approve triggers signature and stores approved proof.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Compact evidence bundle created and stored for 90% of onboarding runs, size median < 6KB.
- Approval UX path completes without engineer assistance in >= 80% of test cohort (internal beta).
- Evidence export to customer S3/webhook occurs within 10s of approval.
- Console shows proof record with minimal summary and link to full logs (if available).

Operational details and telemetry sampling
- Telemetry sampling: sample span traces at 1% by default, 5% for "red" preflight results. Compute a canonical digest (sha256) over sorted key-value pairs: {preflight-summary, changed-routes-hash, ephemeral-agent-version}. Store raw telemetry to internal retention (30 days) and optionally forward to customer endpoint.
- Signature scheme: control-plane signs approval token with ECDSA key v1. Include short key id and timestamp. Token format intentionally short (compact JOSE-ish).

Backward compatibility + migration path
- For customers currently using verbose handoffs: provide a migration helper that creates compact bundles from existing logs by applying our digesting rules. This is an offline script (github link in linked_artifacts).

Security and privacy notes
- Operator identifiers are hashed in exported bundles by default (to preserve privacy in 3rd-party audits). Full identity mapping is available only to named support roles with audit trace.
- Customer can opt to include raw IPs or redact them; explicit toggle during onboarding. Default: redact.

Runbook: failed approval webhooks
- Symptoms: export failed (HTTP 5xx) or S3 put error.
- Immediate: system retries with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts; mark proof record as "export_retry".
- Escalation: after 3 failures, notify operator via email + console banner and attach diagnostic log (short id) to the proof record. Customer success receives a ticket.

Acceptance test ideas
- Synthetic end-to-end: simulate 50 onboarding events across 3 regions; measure bundle sizes, approval latency, export success.
- Security audit: verify signatures are verifiable using control-plane public key.
- UX test: run moderated usability sessions for 8 customers; record time-to-approve and confusion points.

Open questions (short list)
- Should the compact proof include a short human-readable rationale field? (pros: audit-friendly, cons: increases size)
- Is ECDSA sufficient long-term or do we need HSM-backed signing in MVP?
- What is the canonical retention period for compact bundles on control plane (30/90/365 days)?
- How granular should telemetry_digest be to be useful for reconstruction during incident reviews?

Next steps / TODOs
- [ ] Engineering spike: implement generator library (ravi) to produce compact bundles and signature shim (2 wks).
- [ ] UX: prototype approval modal + 3-expander compact view (eleanor) (1 week).
- [ ] Security: review signature format and key lifecycle (diego) (3 days).
- [ ] Ops: draft export retry policy and SLOs, wire to alerts (nina) (1 week).
- [ ] Create internal test harness and synthetic load runner (eng infra).

Notes to self
- Keep the bundle intentionally minimal: think of it as a notarized receipt, not a full report. Customers often need a single artifact to point auditors to.
- Align naming with 'proof' language used in GDPR/compliance playbooks so legal buys in.

References and context
- See linked Confluence page for detailed onboarding checklist mapping.
- Related Jira: PD-5117 for backend work; PD-5220 for UX mockups.
